questions.prompt: Under the Meridian Archive rules: Standard loans last 14 days; Scholar members may renew once for 7 days if no holds exist. Dr. Voss, a Scholar, borrowed a folio on Day 1. On Day 10, a Reader placed a hold. On Day 15, Dr. Voss requests renewal. What occurs?
choices: Renewal denied; hold exists
7-day renewal granted
14-day renewal granted
Item recalled immediately
questions.explanation: Renewal requires no holds and Scholar status. The hold was placed Day 10, before the Day 15 renewal request, so condition fails. Scholar status and 14-day window are irrelevant once hold exists.
questions.expectedAnswer: Renewal denied; hold exists

questions.prompt: Under the Vesper Archive rules: Items loan for 21 days; renewal adds 14 days if borrower has no overdue items and no holds queue. Member Chen has no overdues. On Day 18, a hold is placed on Chen's borrowed atlas. On Day 22, Chen requests renewal. What is the outcome?
choices: Renewal denied; hold exists
14-day extension granted
7-day extension granted
Renewal granted; hold ignored until due date
questions.explanation: Vesper rules require both no overdues AND no holds for renewal. The hold on Day 18 precedes the Day 22 request, blocking renewal. No overdue status is insufficient alone.
questions.expectedAnswer: Renewal denied; hold exists

questions.prompt: Under the Nocturne Archive rules: Loan period is 10 days. Hold precedence: when an item is returned, it goes to the earliest hold requester who is eligible to borrow. Member A (Day 3 hold, Standard member) and Member B (Day 5 hold, Extended member) both request the same journal. Extended members may borrow journals; Standard members may not. The item returns on Day 12. Who receives it?
choices: Member A; earlier hold date
Member B; only eligible borrower
Held for Member A until membership upgrade
Returned to shelves; no valid recipient
questions.explanation: Hold precedence applies only among eligible borrowers. Member A's earlier hold is void due to ineligibility. Member B, though later, is the sole eligible hold requester and receives the item.
questions.expectedAnswer: Member B; only eligible borrower

questions.prompt: Under the Aether Archive rules: Loan window for rare materials is 7 days, non-renewable. Hold precedence uses timestamp only; eligibility is checked at hold placement, not at fulfillment. Member X (eligible, Day 2 hold) and Member Y (eligible, Day 4 hold) both hold the same codex. Member X's account is suspended for overdue fines on Day 5. The codex returns Day 8. Who receives it?
choices: Member Y; earlier eligible hold at fulfillment
Member X; hold precedence locked at placement
Member Y; X's suspension voids their hold
Held for X until account cleared
questions.explanation: Aether rules check eligibility only at hold placement, not fulfillment. Member X was eligible when holding; suspension later does not void the hold. Timestamp precedence gives X the item despite current suspension.
questions.expectedAnswer: Member X; hold precedence locked at placement

questions.prompt: Under the Prism Archive rules: Standard loan is 30 days. Renewal allowed once for 14 days if: (a) request is before due date, (b) no holds exist, AND (c) borrower has fewer than 3 current renewals. Member Park has 2 prior renewals on other items, no holds on her borrowed manuscript due Day 30. She requests renewal on Day 31. What occurs?
choices: Renewal denied; request after due date
14-day renewal granted; under renewal limit
Renewal denied; renewal limit reached
7-day grace renewal granted
questions.explanation: Prism rules require request BEFORE due date. Day 31 request fails condition (a) regardless of holds or renewal count. Other conditions are satisfied but insufficient.
questions.expectedAnswer: Renewal denied; request after due date

questions.prompt: In the Meridian Archive, a Standard member may borrow items for 14 days and renew once for 7 additional days. A Premium member may borrow for 28 days with one 14-day renewal. On Day 1, a Standard member borrows a journal. On Day 10, a Premium member places a hold on that same journal. The Standard member requests renewal on Day 14. What is the outcome?
choices: Renewal denied; the item must be returned by Day 14 due to the active hold.
Renewal granted; the loan extends to Day 21, and the Premium member's hold activates on Day 21.
Renewal granted; the loan extends to Day 28, matching Premium member terms.
Renewal denied; Standard members may not renew items held by Premium members.
questions.explanation: The Standard member's 7-day renewal is permitted because holds only block renewal if placed before the renewal request. The hold was placed on Day 10, before the Day 14 renewal request, so the renewal should be blocked. However, Meridian rules specify holds block renewal only if placed before the original loan expires. Since the hold preceded the renewal request, the renewal is denied and return is due Day 14.
questions.expectedAnswer: Renewal denied; the item must be returned by Day 14 due to the active hold.

questions.prompt: At the Cascade Repository, any member may renew an item exactly once if: (a) no hold exists, and (b) the renewal is requested before the original due date. Due dates are calculated from the renewal request date, not the original due date. A member borrows a map on March 1 with a 21-day loan. On March 20, they request renewal. No holds exist. What is the new due date?
choices: March 21
April 10
March 28
April 11
questions.explanation: The original loan runs March 1–22 (21 days). The March 20 renewal request meets both conditions: before due date and no holds. The new 21-day period runs from March 20, making the new due date April 10.
questions.expectedAnswer: April 10

questions.prompt: The Horizon Archive uses this hold precedence: (1) Institutional members outrank Individual members; (2) among equal ranks, earlier request dates prevail; (3) a member may not borrow an item they already hold. An Institutional member requested Item X on June 1. An Individual member currently borrowing Item X requested a hold on June 3. The Individual member returns Item X on June 5. Who receives it?
choices: The Institutional member; their June 1 request has precedence.
The Individual member; their active hold while borrowing converts to immediate re-loan.
The Individual member; returning triggers automatic renewal instead of hold fulfillment.
Neither; the Individual member's existing loan blocks all holds.
questions.explanation: The Individual member's June 3 hold is invalid under rule (3)—they cannot hold what they borrow. Only the valid Institutional hold exists. Upon return June 5, the Institutional member receives the item.
questions.expectedAnswer: The Institutional member; their June 1 request has precedence.

questions.prompt: In the Vale Library system, loan periods are: Student (7 days), Faculty (56 days). Renewals: Students may renew once for 7 days; Faculty may renew twice for 14 days each. A Faculty member borrows a rare manuscript on September 1. They renew on September 30 and again on October 20. When is the final due date?
choices: November 3
October 27
November 17
December 4
questions.explanation: First loan: September 1–October 27 (56 days). First renewal September 30: new 14-day period runs September 30–October 14. Second renewal October 20: invalid because October 20 is after the October 14 due date. Renewal requests must precede the current due date. Only one renewal applies; final due date is October 27.
questions.expectedAnswer: October 27

questions.prompt: The Sterling Archives operate on rolling midnight deadlines: loans expire at 11:59 PM on the due date. The grace period for return without penalty is 24 hours after expiry. A member borrows equipment at 2:00 PM Monday for 3 days. They attempt renewal at 10:00 PM Thursday. The renewal rule requires the request occur before expiry. What is the outcome?
choices: Renewal granted; the grace period extends the effective expiry to Friday 11:59 PM.
Renewal denied; the loan expired Thursday 11:59 PM, before the 10:00 PM request.
Renewal granted; the request at 10:00 PM Thursday precedes midnight expiry.
Renewal denied; equipment loans prohibit renewal regardless of timing.
questions.explanation: The 3-day loan from Monday 2:00 PM expires Thursday 11:59 PM. The 10:00 PM Thursday request occurs before expiry. The grace period applies only to returns, not renewal eligibility. Renewal is granted.
questions.expectedAnswer: Renewal granted; the request at 10:00 PM Thursday precedes midnight expiry.

questions.prompt: A greenhouse sensor reads 28°C. Policy states: Alert if temperature exceeds 25°C for more than 10 minutes within any 15-minute observation window. The reading has persisted for 8 minutes so far. What action is required?
choices: No alert; duration has not reached the 10-minute threshold
Immediate alert; temperature exceeds 25°C
Alert in 2 minutes when the window closes
Alert only if temperature drops below 25°C first
questions.explanation: The 25°C threshold is exceeded, but the required 10-minute duration within a 15-minute window has not been met (only 8 minutes elapsed). Choice b ignores the duration rule; c invents a window-closing trigger; d contradicts the policy logic.
questions.expectedAnswer: No alert; duration has not reached the 10-minute threshold

questions.prompt: Humidity sensor shows 85% for 12 minutes. Policy: Alert if humidity exceeds 80% for at least 15 continuous minutes. A maintenance override flag is active, which pauses all humidity alerts. What action is required?
choices: No alert; the maintenance override takes precedence
Alert; the threshold condition will soon be satisfied
Alert; the override does not apply to 85% readings
No alert; the observation window has not closed
questions.explanation: The override explicitly pauses humidity alerts regardless of sensor values or duration progress. Choice b ignores the override; c invents an exception; d confuses window closure with the override rule.
questions.expectedAnswer: No alert; the maintenance override takes precedence

questions.prompt: CO2 reads 1200 ppm. Policy: Alert if CO2 exceeds 1000 ppm for more than 5 minutes within a 20-minute observation window. The reading has been 1200 ppm for exactly 6 minutes. What action is required?
choices: Immediate alert; threshold exceeded for required duration within window
No alert; wait until 20 minutes elapse
No alert; 1200 ppm is within acceptable variance
Alert only if CO2 drops below 1000 ppm first
questions.explanation: 1200 ppm exceeds 1000 ppm, and the 6-minute duration exceeds the 5-minute minimum within the 20-minute window. Choice b misinterprets the window as a waiting period; c invents a variance rule; d reverses the threshold logic.
questions.expectedAnswer: Immediate alert; threshold exceeded for required duration within window

questions.prompt: Temperature is 22°C (threshold: 25°C). Humidity is 75% (threshold: 80%). A manual override states: "If temperature is below threshold, ignore humidity alerts." Humidity has exceeded 80% for 20 minutes. What action is required?
choices: No alert; the temperature condition triggers the override
Immediate humidity alert; duration threshold satisfied
Temperature alert; humidity is near threshold
Both alerts; overrides apply separately to each sensor
questions.explanation: The override explicitly conditions humidity alert suppression on temperature being below threshold, which is true (22°C < 25°C). Choice b ignores the override; c invents a temperature alert; d misreads the override scope.
questions.expectedAnswer: No alert; the temperature condition triggers the override

questions.expectedAnswer: No alert; the scheduled override is active

Frost Alert
Both Irrigation Alert and Frost Alert
No alert

questions.prompt: Greenhouse Policy Rule: Trigger Humidity Alert if relative humidity exceeds 80% for two consecutive 10-minute readings. Current readings at 9:00, 9:10, 9:20: 78%, 82%, 79%. What is required?

Suppress CO2 Alert due to override
Trigger CO2 Alert and clear the flag
Wait 5 minutes then reassess
questions.explanation: CO2 at 1350 ppm exceeds 1200 ppm threshold, but the Manual Override Rule explicitly suppresses CO2 Alert when 'Ventilation Active' is set. Choice a ignores the override. Choice c violates the suppression instruction. Choice d invents a timing rule not stated.

questions.prompt: Greenhouse Policy Rule: Light Alert triggers if PAR (photosynthetically active radiation) is below 200 µmol/m²/s for 30 continuous minutes. Current PAR readings each minute for 35 minutes: 25 minutes at 180, then 10 minutes at 220. What is required?

Light Alert in 5 more minutes if PAR stays low
No Light Alert based on current data
Light Alert triggered at minute 30

Choice a misreads the duration. Choice b assumes future data. Choice d incorrectly treats minute 30 as sufficient without checking continuity.

Both Temperature Alert and Emergency Evacuation
No alert; wait for Fire Suppression activation
